- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >0.5), model overreacts; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 0.1–0.3 per day for next 5 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 1.5), model tends to hold high; apply “mean reversion bias” — cap forecast at 1.5–2.0 for next 3 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply “horizon decay” — reduce forecast by 5–15% for days 1–7, then stabilize.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model may misread momentum; use “sentiment cycle” — adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction, not absolute value.
